# DDoS IP Blocker Script
# This script checks incoming network traffic against a list of known attacker IP addresses
# and blocks any matches for 24 hours. It also logs blocked IP addresses and the time they were blocked.
# The script is designed to be deployed on a Linux system using iptables.

# Configuration variables
BLOCK_DURATION=86400  # 24 hours in seconds
LOG_FILE="/var/log/ddos_block.log"
IP_LIST_FILE="/etc/ddos/ip_list.txt"
BLOCK_RULES_FILE="/etc/ddos/block_rules.txt"

# Function to check if an IP address is in the known attacker list

    local ip=$1
    grep -q "^$ip$" "$IP_LIST_FILE" >/dev/null 2>&1
    return $?
}

# Function to block an IP address for 24 hours
block_ip() {
    local ip=$1
    local timestamp=$(date +%s)
    echo "Blocked IP: $ip at $timestamp" >> "$LOG_FILE"
    iptables -A INPUT -s $ip -j DROP
    echo "Rule added: DROP from $ip" >> "$BLOCK_RULES_FILE"

    local ip=$1
    iptables -D INPUT -s $ip -j DROP
    echo "Rule removed: DROP from $ip" >> "$BLOCK_RULES_FILE"
}

# Main script execution

    # Read incoming network traffic and check for blocked IPs
    for ip in $(netstat -an | grep LISTEN | awk '{print $5}' | cut -d: -f1 | sort -u); do

            block_ip "$ip"
        fi
    done
    
    # Sleep for 1 hour to reduce CPU usage

rotate_logs() {
    # Create a new log file with a timestamp
    TIMESTAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)
    NEW_LOG_FILE="$LOG_DIR/network_$TIMESTAMP.log"
    
    # Copy the current log file to the new one
    cp "$LOG_DIR/network.log" "$NEW_LOG_FILE"
    
    # Remove the old log file
    rm "$LOG_DIR/network.log"
    
    # Rename the new log file to the old one

}

# Function to parse logs and identify threats
parse_logs() {
    # Read each log file in the directory
    for file in "$LOG_DIR"/*.log; do

            while IFS= read -r line; do

    if [[ $line =~ ^[0-9]{1,3}\.[0-9]{1,3}\.[0-9]{1,3}\.[0-9]{1,3} ]]; then
